transcript.text: “Won’t come on” can mean either completely dead, or powered up but refusing to start. The quickest split is whether there are any lights. 1. Check the plug and the switched spur/socket feeding the dishwasher are fully on. If safe to do so, try another appliance in that socket. If the circuit has tripped, do not keep resetting it. A dead socket points to the supply rather than the dishwasher. 2. If the display does light, open the door and check no rack, tall plate or cutlery is preventing it closing. Shut it firmly until it clicks, select a programme and press Start. If it has power but will not start, the door latch/interlock or a control/delay lock are more likely. 3. Look for a padlock/key symbol or a delay countdown such as “3h”. A child lock or delay start can make the buttons seem unresponsive; the manual shows the button combination to cancel the lock. When you open the door, are there any lights or display at all, and does another appliance work from the dishwasher socket?
No lights or display at all, totally dead. Other sockets and lights in the kitchen work. The spur switch above the worktop is on and its little light is lit.

A lit spur switch only shows that the switch itself has a supply; it does not prove power is getting through to the dishwasher. The most likely split now is a blown spur fuse/output fault, or an internal mains-input/control-board fault. 1. Turn off the dishwasher circuit at the consumer unit first — do not rely on the spur switch alone.
2. Open the small fuse drawer in the spur and inspect the fuse. Replace it only with the same rating printed on the old fuse or spur; never fit a higher-rated one.
3. Restore power once. If the new fuse blows, or there is any burning smell, heat or discolouration, leave it off and arrange an electrician/appliance engineer. If the fuse is intact and the dishwasher remains completely dead, the fault is more likely inside the appliance, typically its mains input connection or control/power board. That needs an engineer rather than internal DIY work.
I don't know how to check the fuse and I haven't got a spare or a meter. Nothing's tripped at the consumer unit. Can't pull the dishwasher out either. What now?

The sensible next step is to arrange an electrician or appliance engineer rather than trying to dismantle anything yourself. There is no further useful owner-safe check if you cannot access the appliance or check the fused spur. The illuminated spur only proves it has an incoming supply. The engineer needs to establish whether power is leaving the spur and reaching the dishwasher. The two realistic causes are: 1. A blown fuse or failed connection/output in the fused spur.
2. If the spur output is live, an internal dishwasher mains-input connection or power/control board fault. Ask the visit engineer to test the spur output first before condemning dishwasher parts. That avoids paying for an internal repair if the fault is simply the fused connection above the worktop. Do not keep switching it on and off, and leave it isolated if there is any heat, burning smell or discolouration around the spur.

candidates: Power supply, plug, switched spur or fuse issue (high)
Door not closing or door latch/interlock not recognising the door as shut (medium)
Control lock, delay start or programme selection (medium)

tags.checkGiven: Check the dishwasher's plug is fully in and its socket or the switched spur (often a switch above the worktop) is on, and try another applia

plan: The fault they reported is: "won't come on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
